new_statements.quote: Et ords trykforhold fremgår langthen af opslagsformen. (1) I et usammensat ord hviler hovedtrykket normalt på første stavelse; hvis ikke, særmarkeres dette i opslagsformen med ˈ (hævet trykstreg) foran den stavelse, der bærer hovedtrykket (se fx beˈtale, aˈpril, alteˈreret); hermed signaleres samtidig, at den el. de forudgående stavelser er helt tryksvage. (2) Et sammensat ord har normalt hovedtryk på 1.sms.led, bitryk på 2.sms.led, hvilket i opslagsformen antydes med skilletegnet · (hævet punktum) mellem de to led (se fx bred·skuldret, jule·aften).
new_statements.translation: A word's stress pattern is largely apparent from the headword form. (1) In a non-compound word the main stress normally rests on the first syllable; if not, this is specially marked in the headword form with ˈ (raised stress mark) before the syllable that bears the main stress (see e.g. beˈtale 'pay', aˈpril, alteˈreret 'agitated'); this at the same time signals that the preceding syllable(s) are completely unstressed. (2) A compound word normally has main stress on the first member and secondary stress on the second member, which the headword form indicates with the separator · (raised dot) between the two members (see e.g. bred·skuldret 'broad-shouldered', jule·aften 'Christmas Eve').
new_statements.citation: Jysk Ordbog. Peter Skautrup Centret for Jysk Dialektforskning, Aarhus Universitet (founded by Peter Skautrup 1932; editors Peter Skautrup, Ove Rasmussen, Viggo Sørensen, Torben Arboe, Inger Schoonderbeek Hansen, Nina Grøftehauge, Mette-Marie Møller Svendsen, Kristoffer Friis Bøegh; web-published since 2000, web edition 2017, last update Jan 2025). After stripping the HTML tags (the ˈ sits inside in the raw markup) the reader's quote from "Et ords trykforhold fremgår langthen af opslagsformen." through "(se fx bred·skuldret, jule·aften)." is an exact substring of the page text; the paragraph is followed by "Yderligere el. afvigende information om trykforholdet må søges i evt. sideformer og/eller i de anførte lydformer." Translation is accurate. Reading: the source says main stress "normalt på første stavelse" in simplex words with non-initial stress marked individually (beˈtale, aˈpril, alteˈreret) and compoun…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary stress falls on the first syllable of a simplex word by default; words with unstressed prefixes or loanwords (beˈtale, aˈpril, alteˈreret) carry stress on a later syllable and are marked individually, i.e. the exceptions are lexical, of the ordinary Danish type. Compounds take main stress on the first member and secondary stress on the second. This is the same Germanic root-initial pattern that the 19th-century grammars state by reference to Standard Danish: Varming 1862 §56 p. 20 'Med Tonefaldet i usammensatte Ord forholder det sig sædvanlig som i Dansk' and Hagerup 1854 §33 p. 100 / Hagerup-Lyngby 1867 §33 p. 132 'Hovedtonen falder i den angelske Mundart på samme Stavelse som i Sprogets øvrige Skikkelser'; Feilberg 1886 (p. IX-X) marks main stress only 'når hovedtonen falder andensteds end på første stavelse'.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Compounds: main stress on the first member, secondary stress (bitryk) on the second member (Jysk Ordbog, Udtale (2)). The dictionary's sign list (Hjælp > Lydtegn) adds a 'svagtryk' sign ° for an unexpectedly weak stress on the following syllable, with dialect examples sydøstjysk ˈfar·°brə 'farbror', thybomål ˈdaw·lə°stòw 'dagligstue'. Varming 1862 §56 notes that certain derivational suffixes take a stronger secondary stress (Årmud, Hjåwhid) and that words of more than two syllables mostly have the stress on the penult because the final syllable has been apocopated (Agend for Agende, Drikkels for Drikkelse); §57: in compound nouns either both members are stressed with main stress on the first, or one member loses its stress.
new_statements.exceptions: Jysk Ordbog: simplex words with non-initial stress (prefixed verbs and loans such as beˈtale, aˈpril, alteˈreret) are marked individually. Varming 1862 §57 pp. 20-21: some compounds stress the last member (Godaw, Goldtc, grangivvelle, fuldkommele; many place names in -gor, -land, -eng, -bro, -holm, -ma); adjectives usually lose stress on the last member (gråblå); §58 p. 21: prefixes as in Danish, for- stressed as preposition (Fórbin) but unstressed as mere prefix (forhast), u- stressed before monosyllables (úlykk) but not in ulykkele. Hagerup 1854 §33 p. 100 / 1867 §33 p. 132 (Angel dialect): only a few compounds deviate by stressing the last member (Forskjel, Ungkarl, Kirkeværge, Altermand, Søskendebarn, undvære, omgåes, sometimes Farsøster, Morsøster); §34: compound place names very often stress the last member (Bondebro, Engbro, Helligbæk..), but names in -ager, -balle, -berg, -bjerg, -by, -bøl, -gab, -holt, -høj, -lev, -nes, -rød, -rup, -strup, -sted, -toft, -ved stress the first member; §35: secondary stress is often lost in compounds (Kobås, Kromand, Kalgår). Prosody beyond stress: most Jutish dialects have stød (West Jutish stød on short vowels/consonants, 'klusilspring' in Vendsyssel), while Als/Sundeved/Rømø have tonal accent 1 vs 2 (Jysk Ordbog Lydtegn: ˹ marks tonal accent 2, e.g. alsisk ˹hu·s 'huse' vs hu·s 'hus').
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level stress in citation (headword) forms; the dictionary describes the Jutlandic dialects of ca. 1700-1930 (bulk of sources 1850-1920), all areas of Jutland and South Schleswig. Varming 1862 §67 Anm. additionally notes that in connected speech words lose their 'Tonehold' under sentence accent ('Sætningsbetoningen, den oratoriske Accent'), i.e. a separate phrase-level phenomenon.
new_statements.identity_note: The deciding source (Jysk Ordbog, Peter Skautrup Centret, Aarhus University) covers all Jutlandic dialects (Nørrejysk and Sønderjysk incl. South Schleswig) as spoken ca. 1700-1930, i.e. the whole of juti1236. Supporting older primaries: Varming 1862 covers Jutish in general; Hagerup 1854 / Hagerup-Lyngby 1867 describe only the Angel (Angeln, South Schleswig) dialect, an extinct South Jutish variety (no separate Glottolog code known to me; subsumed under juti1236); Feilberg 1886 is the general Jutish dictionary. Note that Glottolog's 'phonology' entry Andersen 1958 (Fonemsystemet i Østfynsk) describes East Funen Danish, not Jutish, and was not pursued.

Tegnet for Hovedtonen er her (´). — Enkelte Afledsendelser faa dog en stærkere Bitone.. ligesom ogsaa Ord af flere end to Stavelser oftest have Tonen paa næstsidste, idet den sidste er bortfaldt' — i.e. stress placement as in Danish (root-initial); §57 compounds: main stress on the first member, with listed exceptions stressing the last member; §58 prefixes as in Danish; §§59-67 the 'Tonehold' (stød / drawling tone) system.
